indicator_assessments.description: IDC, Counterpoint, Gartner revise forecasts down (the quantity signal) PLUS the leading price-pass-through edge — OEMs raising end-device prices or cutting memory content to offset memory costs.
indicator_assessments.what_to_look_for: QUANTITY (firing condition, already met): IDC PC shipment forecast revised to -5% or worse for 2026 (current -2.4 to -11.3% — already fired). Counterpoint smartphone <0% (current -2%). Gartner data center server forecast cut. LEADING / INTENSIFICATION (signal already fired — these DEEPEN it, they are the early end-market tell before forecast cuts widen): OEMs raising end-device prices to offset memory costs (Apple, Microsoft, Sony, Nintendo, Dell, Valve), removing low-spec/entry configurations, cutting memory content per device, substituting cheaper nodes, or delaying refresh cycles. indicator_assessments.name: DRAM Price Evolution (spot + contract matrix)
indicator_assessments.description: 5x5 trigger matrix mapping DRAM contract QoQ growth (rows) against DDR5 16Gb 4800/5600 spot drawdown from rolling 12-week peak (cols). Returns Not fired / Partially fired / Fired per cell. Replaces the v3.39 absolute-threshold trigger ($38.2 spot / $950 module). The matrix is the framework's canonical early-warning signal — spot drawdown leads contract direction by 6-10 weeks. Matrix engine: src/data/cycle_matrix.py; charts: src/analysis/chart_generator.py.
indicator_assessments.what_to_look_for: Today's cell position on the 5x5 matrix. ROWS (contract QoQ): R1 >=+30%, R2 +20-30%, R3 +10-20%, R4 +5-10%, R5 <=+5%. COLS (spot drawdown from rolling 12w peak): C1 at peak, C2 <5% off, C3 5-10% off, C4 10-20% off, C5 >=20% off. Not fired = R1/R2 with low drawdown (full position). Partially fired = mid-band (review thesis, consider 25-33% trim). Fired = any R4-R5 row, any C5 column, or R3+C4. Historical cycle peaks all landed in R5 by the time contract growth hit ~0% — the matrix exists to act BEFORE that. Contract row uses a SYNTHETIC estimate: anchor (most recent TrendForce quarterly forecast, preferring server_ddr5 > conventional_dram_aggregate segments) + 0.4 * tone_adj + 0.4 * supplier_adj + 0.2 * spot_lead_adj, each capped +/-30pp.
indicator_assessments.where_we_stand: Cell: Not fired (Row 1 x Col 1). No firing condition met — hold full position. DDR5 16Gb 4800/5600 spot $48.57 (2026-07-15 print). Matrix basis (weekly means): current wk $48.47, +0.00% vs rolling 12w wk-peak $48.47 (wk ending 2026-07-19). 0w since last new peak. Contract anchor: Q2_2026 58-63% QoQ (trendforce_press_release, published 2026-03-31, 106d old). Synthetic adjusted: 51.1% central (range 49-54%). Adjustments: tone +4.1pp (11 src, weight 0.4); supplier -30.0pp (1 src, weight 0.4); spot_lead +5.0pp (1 src, weight 0.2).

indicator_assessments.what_to_look_for: SK Hynix (000660.KS) or Micron (MU) underperforms SOX (^SOX) by >10% over 5 trading days. Currently fired then reversed (Mar 2026 fired, May rally erased).
indicator_assessments.where_we_stand: 5-day vs SOX: SK Hynix -16.97pp (RED — threshold -10pp), Micron -0.57pp (below yellow threshold). DRAM ETF vs SMH 5d: -8.43pp (DRAM -11.52%, SMH -3.09% — yellow watch). Severity: red. SK Hynix's -16.97pp spread is the dominant driver; the Q2 earnings miss and ADR pricing overhang are the proximate causes of the divergence from the broader semi tape. Micron's near-flat spread (-0.57pp) confirms this is SK Hynix-specific, not a broad memory underperformance. The DRAM ETF yellow flag (-8.43pp) adds a secondary confirmation. Prior status was Not fired (recovered May 2026)…
indicator_assessments.latest_developments: SK Hynix ADR dropped ~10% post-Q2 miss (2026-07-13), driving the 5-day spread to -16.97pp vs SOX. WDC, Micron, SanDisk fell 6%+ in sympathy. KIS analyst flagged HBM price surge showing signs of cooling — directional…

indicator_assessments.name: Supplier inventory rebuilds 2-3 → 4-5 weeks
indicator_assessments.description: Memory makers' inventory weeks rising from record lows.
indicator_assessments.what_to_look_for: SK Hynix or Micron inventory weeks crossing 4 in TrendForce monthly print or earnings disclosure. Currently 2-3 weeks.
indicator_assessments.where_we_stand: Not fired. Supplier inventory weeks remain at 2–3 weeks per TrendForce Q3 2025 baseline; no subsequent print has crossed the 4-week trigger threshold. ASML's 2026 memory revenue +75% and SK Hynix's HBM capacity reallocation (per Mirae Jul 14–15) are consistent with continued tight supplier inventory — HBM allocation crowds out DDR5 wafers, keeping finished-goods weeks low. No earnings disclosure from SK Hynix or Micron today. Next read: SK Hynix Q2 2026 earnings (expected late Jul 2026).
indicator_assessments.latest_developments: No new inventory weeks data today. Mirae (Jul 14–15) confirms HBM capacity prioritization consistent with tight supplier inventory. Trigger threshold (4 weeks) not approached.

indicator_assessments.name: CapEx slashed
indicator_assessments.description: Memory makers announce major CapEx cuts.
indicator_assessments.what_to_look_for: Any Big Three announces CapEx reduction of >20% or fab idling.
indicator_assessments.where_we_stand: No CapEx cuts announced by SK Hynix, Micron, or Samsung today. Samsung fast-tracked Yongin fab to 2029 — the opposite of a cut. SK Hynix KRW 7.35T capacity allocation stands. Trigger requires >20% CapEx reduction or fab idling — not in evidence.
indicator_assessments.latest_developments: Samsung accelerated Yongin fab timeline to 2029. No CapEx cuts from any Big Three member.
